summary:
Protomars is an interactive space exploration and mission command platform designed to bridge terrestrial analog testing with orbital mechanics education.
   What We Developed: We built a unified web application featuring an interactive topographical Aresanalog Map for Martian surface analysis alongside Ares New Eden, a structured three-phase simulation campaign. The campaign spans Earth atmospheric trials and VTOL descents (an1, tructhang, an3, tuyen1), lunar gateway transit logistics (an2), and Martian colonization protocols (tuyen2, tructhang2).
   How It Solves the Challenge: It gamifies and visualizes complex aerospace engineering challenges, transforming abstract orbital and descent mechanics into intuitive, hands-on digital simulations.
     Why It Matters: Protomars provides an accessible, immersive training pipeline, empowering students and researchers to visualize mission architecture and inspire the next generation of space explorers for Red Planet colonization.
details:
Detailed Project Description: Protomars

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Protomars is a unified, web-based space exploration and mission command platform that merges topographical mapping with a structured operational campaign.

  • Aresanalog Map: Functions as an interactive topographical simulation tool of Martian terrain and analog testing zones, allowing users to analyze surface geography and mission hazards.
    • Mission 1 (Earth Terrestrial Trials): Covers atmospheric entry and thermal shielding (an1), vertical descent and VTOL hover calibration (tructhang), subterranean core drilling (an3), and orbital trajectory/gravity assist mechanics (tuyen1).
    • Mission 2 (Lunar Transit Station): Manages low-gravity docking maneuvers and orbital logistics on the Moon (an2).
    • Mission 3 (Mars Colonization & Ascent): Simulates deep-space interplanetary transfer (tuyen2) and final surface base landing and modular habitat deployment (tructhang2). Users navigate through a secure web command hub (index.html) deployed on Netlify, launching interactive HTML5/JS simulations seamlessly.

2. What benefits does it provide?

  • Educational Accessibility: Translates complex aerospace engineering, orbital mechanics, and descent physics into intuitive, gamified digital simulations.
  • Risk-Free Prototyping: Serves as a digital analog testing environment to visualize mission phases before physical deployment.
  • Streamlined UX: Provides a frictionless experience where all mission components are centralized into a single, responsive, space-themed command interface without requiring external logins or bulky installations.

3. What is the expected impact of the project?

  • Inspiring the Next Generation: Engages students, space enthusiasts, and young learners in STEM by making interplanetary colonization concepts tangible and exciting.
  • Open-Access Analog Tool: Offers an accessible web framework that educators and researchers can use as a baseline for teaching orbital mechanics and mission planning.
  • Community Engagement: Fosters interest in space exploration datasets and analog astronautics through immersive web experiences.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Frontend Development: HTML5, CSS3 (with responsive custom grid layouts, canvas particle animations, and glassmorphism UI), and JavaScript (ES6+ for state management and DOM manipulation).
  • Hosting & Deployment: Netlify (for high-availability cloud deployment and global public link distribution).
  • Assets & Maps: Custom interactive HTML/JS simulation files (an1, tructhang, an3, tuyen1, an2, tuyen2, tructhang2, and aresanalog) integrated into a unified hub.

5. How innovative is your project?

Protomars innovates by bridging topographical mapping and sequential mission training into a cohesive web ecosystem. Instead of isolated educational tools, it creates a narrative-driven "Ares New Eden" campaign that guides users logically from Earth testing all the way to Martian settlement. Its lightweight, zero-install architecture ensures that anyone with a browser can instantly experience aerospace simulation.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • User Experience & Accessibility: Ensuring the interface is lightweight, fast-loading, and compatible across modern browsers via cloud hosting while keeping navigation intuitive.
  • Modular Scalability: Designing the directory structure and main hub logic so that individual simulation modules operate smoothly and can be expanded or updated independently.
  • Thematic Immersion: Crafting a professional, sci-fi aesthetic (deep space dark mode combined with Martian red-orange gradients and starfield animations) to match the gravity and excitement of space exploration.
